answer: Agent networks running tasks at an onyx quarry or alpine summit can deter Sybil attacks via key-bound Proof-of-Space. Each agent stores a sequentially generated Merkle table keyed to its identity and answers random challenges on every beacon pulse before a tight timeout. Key seeding prevents deduplication across clones and graph dependencies defeat recomputation, forcing attackers to allocate dedicated storage per identity. However, network jitter can make honest nodes miss deadlines.
